Author: Hirdesh
Bench: Hirdesh
 1
 In The High Court Of Madhyapradesh
 At G Wa L I O R
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Hirdesh
 On The 13th Of September, 2024
Miscellaneous Appeal No. 224 Of 2014

Smt. Rani And Others
 Versus
 Anupam Kumar And Others

Appearance:
Ms. Meena Singhal, learned counsel for appellants.
Shri Bhagwan Das Verma- learned counsel for respondent No.3.
Shri Somyadeep Dwivedi- learned Proxy Counsel on behalf of Shri Shrinivas
Gajendragadkar- Counsel for respondent No.3- Insurance Company.

Present Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is directed against the Award dated 26 th of November, 2013 passed by Member, 10th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (in short ''Claims Tribunal'') Gwalior in Claim Case No.169 of 2013, whereby compensation of Rs.5,60,000/- has been awarded in favour of the claimants (appellants herein), holding contributory negligence of the deceased to the extent of 25% in the alleged accident.
(2) Briefly stated facts of case are on 22-08-2011, deceased- Santosh was returning to Raj Hotel with one Suraj Khatik on his motorcycle No. MP07-MA- 9998 where he used to work.

entities.text: 10th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (in short ''Claims Tribunal'') Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As soon as he reached in front of Forest Department, AB Road Ghatigaon, respondent No.2 who was driving offending vehicle Travera No. MP07-BA-2111 in very rash and negligent manner, came on wrong side and dashed motorcycle due to which, Santosh and Suraj sustained serious injuries.
On the basis of which, Crime No.119 of 2009 was registered at PS Ghatigaon, District Gwalior.
Santosh was admitted in JA Hospital, Hospital where he was declared dead.

The dependents (herein appellants)
of deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal on the ground that at the time of accident, Santosh was hale and hearty 22 years old young man and used to work as cook in Raj Hotel situated at Ghatigaon owned by Shailendra Rathore and from where he used to get monthly salary of Rs.6,000/- per month.
Apart from this, deceased used to earn additional income of Rs.4,000/- per month by cooking at marriage party.

Present appellants Smt. Rani vs Anupam Kumar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53779691/
1 are his dependents and they are entitled to get Rs.32,40,000/- as compensation.
(3) Respondents No.1 & 2 (owner and driver of offending vehicle) filed reply to claim petition stating that death of deceased- Santosh was not caused by offending vehicle.
Deceased himself was driving motorcycle very fast and carelessly and overtook the truck going ahead of him and came on wrong side and fell on ground due to which alleged accident had taken place.
At the time of accident, the offending car was insured with the Insurance Company and, hence, the Insurance Company is fully liable to pay compensation.

(4) The Insurance Company also filed reply to claim petition denying the fact that deceased died in motorcycle accident and the alleged accident had happened due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle and deceased was also responsible for the accident on the ground that he was crossing road by keeping wooden logs on both sides of his motorcycle due to which, he lost his balance and accident occurred.
The Insurance Company further alleged that the driver of offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving licence which is in violation of provisions of policy.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.

(5) On the basis of pleadings of both the parties and documents available therein, the Claims Tribunal framed issues and awarded compensation of Rs.5,60,000/- in favour of the claimants holding that the deceased was also responsible for the accident fixing his contributory negligence to the extent of 25%.
(6) Challenging the impugned Award, learned Counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal has committed a grave error by determining 25% of contributory negligence on the part of deceased on the basis of spot map Ex.D2 whereas, AW-2 Kishan Adiwasi, in his statement stated that at the time of accident, deceased was coming on right side towards Raj Hotel driving his motorcycle slowly and at that time, driver of offending vehicle was coming from Gwalior driving the vehicle very fast and carelessly on wrong side and dashed motorcycle due to which deceased suffered serious injuries and died on spot.

Learned Claims Tribunal also committed an error in not considering the documentary and oral evidence produced on behalf of claimants regarding income of deceased and has wrongly assessed income of deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month.
(7) Heard learned Counsel for parties and perused the record as well as impugned Award.

(8) The main question for determination is as to whether the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in drawing assumption that on the basis of spot map Ex.D2 deceased was contributory negligent to the extent of 25% for the alleged accident or not ?
(9) Kishan Adiwasi (AW-2) in his statement deposed that deceased was coming towards Raj Hotel from Ghatigaon side on his motorcycle slowly and Suraj was sitting on motorcycle.

As soon as the motorcycle reached in front of Forest Department, the offending vehicle, which was coming from Gwalior driven by respondent No.2 recklessly and negligently in very high speed, came on wrong side and dashed the motorcycle due to which, deceased fell down with motorcycle and suffered severe injuries and died on spot.
This witness in Para 6 of his cross- examination fairly stated that at the time of accident, deceased was coming from Shivpuri towards Raj Hotel.
He further denied that deceased turned his motorcycle towards Raj Hotel.
This witness further admitted that police had prepared spot map Ex.D2.

In Para 14 of his cross-examination, he further stated that the driver of Smt. Rani vs Anupam Kumar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53779691/
2 offending vehicle came on the side of deceased and dashed motorcycle by driving very rashly and negligently.

This witness further in Para 15 of his cross- examination denied the fact that deceased was driving motorcycle very fast and recklessly, crossed the road and came on wrong side due to which accident had taken place.
He further denied that deceased was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
This witness further denied that accident occurred due to wooden log kept on motorcycle by deceased and due to unbalance of motorcycle.
(10) On perusal of record, it appears that the driver of offending vehicle was solely responsible for alleged accident as he was driving the vehicle in vary rashly and negligently.
There was no evidence on record to suggest any negligence on the part of the deceased.
Spot map (Ex.D2) also does not suggest any rash and negligent driving on the part of the deceased.
When evidence of AW2- Kishan Adiwasi and also FIR are also on record and there was no contrary evidence, the Claims Tribunal was not justified in merely drawing assumption based on spot map (Ex.D2).
Apart from this, the Investigating Officer has also not been called in evidence to prove spot map (Ex.D2).
Therefore, no definite opinion can be given that the deceased was driving the motorcycle rashly and negligently at the time of accident.
Mere suspicion based on spot map cannot take place of evidence, particularly when direct evidence of AW2- Kisan Adiwasi is on record.

(11) In the case of Jiju Kuruvila & Others vs. Kunjujamma Mohan & Others 2013 ACJ 2141, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Para 24 has observed that the mere position of the vehicles after accident, as shown in a scene mahazar, cannot give a substantial proof as to rash and negligent driving on the part of one or the other.

entities.text: Jiju Kuruvila & Others vs. Kunjujamma Mohan & Others 2013 ACJ 2141
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When two vehicles coming from opposite directions collide, the position of the vehicles and their directions, etc, depends on a number of factors like speed of vehicles, intensity of collision, reason for collision, place at which one vehicle hit the other, etc.

From the scene of the accident, one may suggest or presume the manner in which accident occurred, but in absence of any direct or corroborative evidence, no conclusion can be drawn as to whether there was negligence on the part of the driver.
In absence of such direct or corroborative evidence, the Court cannot give any specific finding about negligence on the part of any individual.

(12) On perusal of evidence of witness AW2- Kishan Adiwasi, it appears that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in holding contributory negligence of the deceased to the extent of 25% in the alleged accident and the finding given by the Claims Tribunal appears to be incorrect in law and is, accordingly modified to the extent that the driver of offending vehicle is solely responsible for alleged accident.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally responsible to pay compensation.
(13) So far as the question of quantum of compensation is concerned, no reliable evidence has been adduced by claimants that deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- per month by working as cook in Raj Hotel.

Although the Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month on notional basis, however, as per the minimum wages, on the date of accident, minimum wage of an unskilled person should have been Rs.4,545/- per month.
Accordingly, the income of deceased is assessed at Rs.4,545/- per month.

(14) So far as the contention of appellants that at the time of death of deceased his age was 22 years and there are six dependents on deceased (appellant No.1- wife, appellant No.2-mother, appellant No.3-father, appellants no. 4 and 6- sisters and appellant No.5- brother of deceased) is concerned,
in the considered opinion of this Court, only wife and mother are the sole dependents and,
therefore, 1/3 rd deduction from the income of deceased is to be made towards personal and living Smt. Rani vs Anupam Kumar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53779691/
3 expenses and looking to the age of deceased as 22 years, the Claims Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 18.

As regards future prospect, as the deceased was not a Government servant, in the light of decision of Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi,
reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the claimants are entitled for future prospect @ 40%.

sentences.text:
Besides the aforesaid, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of consortium,
a sum of Rs.18,150/- towards loss of estate and a sum of Rs. 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT

Monthly income Rs. 4,545/-
 Dependency

(after deduction of 1/3 rd  towards personal and living expenses towards) Rs. 3,030/-
 Income (Rs.3,030/- pm x 12 months) Rs. 36,360/-
 40% towards future prospect Rs. 14,544/-
 Income + future prospect (Rs.36,360 + Rs.14,544) Rs. 50,904/-
 Multiplier 18 Rs. 9,16,272/-
 Other heads:-
Loss of consortium (wife, mother and father = Rs.48,400/-x3) Rs. 1,45,200/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 18,150/-
 Loss of expenses Rs. 18,150/-
 Total= Rs. 10,97,772/-
(15)
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.10,97,772/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.5,60,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.5,37,772/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
(16) With aforesaid modification, this miscellaneous appeal is disposed off by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.5,37,772/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

(17) Appellants- claimants have valued the appeal only Rs.3 lac and paid Court fees, however, for remaining amount above Rs.3 lac, Court fee shall be paid by appellants within a period of one month and thereafter, aforesaid enhanced amount shall be released by Insurance Company on receiving the information of deposit of Court fee by appellants.
In case, the Court fees has not been deposited before the Court until the period of three months, appellants shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhance amount of compensation.
